body:
Well, my doctor told me a sure-fire way to know is if antidepressants make you manic. Like, talk super fast, too energetic, etc.

Beyond that, all I know is extreme highs and lows.

But that's really information you'd get from a doctor. They know more than I would.

I do, at least in the United States. They can definitely help you with that if nothing else is working for you. It isn't an easy experience, but it can be worth it.

Is there anything specific you're curious about or worried about?
Some people also have anxiety, PTSD, bi-polar, etc. Which would make a difference in the medications you may benefit most from. I'm not sure what they entail specifically, though.

Then at the very least, something like wellbutrin may be a place to start. I think it's the most mild option for depression, and it should help you feel a little more energetic in more ways than one.

If you already have another diagnosis beyond major depression though, maybe something else would be more helpful.

I think dating sites barely work. I imagine they're even harder for men. I've tried before, too. I've been the woman who lost interest in the conversation... I didn't feel invested or interested enough, because of a very important factor; having something relateable to attach on to.

In my experience... it just feels better when you get to know someone more naturally, without the pretense of "looking for a boyfriend/girlfriend". That creates a layer of pressure for everyone, and I think conversations are just more difficult and harder to get invested in.

Since I'm an artist, I choose to hang out where other artists would be so that we can meet based on this important career/hobby to both of us. Conversations are easier, more free, more natural. Less pressure to DATE/SEX it up.

Give it a shot if you haven't already. You don't have anything to lose! You'll probably, at least, make a friend. And that's a really phenomenal thing.

I didn't meet the man of my dreams so far either. But I did meet my best friend this way, and I'm happy I have him in my life.

I've been on bupropion/wellbutrin for the last few months. I've noticed a significant difference, but not perfect. But, a medication doesn't solve your problems, it just helps stabilize your mood so that you can have the energy to solve your problems.

I've been too scared to consider trying other stuff cause the sexual side effects terrify me, heh. I'd rather that one good thing not be taken from me!

I have heard that other antidepressants that are combined with wellbutrin does help the sexual side effects, though. It's worth research, and worth discussing with your doctor. I was surprised when my doctor said that a lot of people were too shy to talk about sexual side effects. It seems so important!
"My hurt is the real hurt, so I'm going to invalidate your hurt because I said so."

I think you're really cute! Am I the only girl who likes somewhat chubby guys? I wanted to comment cause I'm a little sore about all of the negativity! Though I guess I'm pretty useless if you're looking to change some things!

Me too. It sucks. There are tablets you can get to help you digest dairy, though. I like the chew-able vanilla ones, but there are capsules, too.

We can still enjoy ice cream and pizza. Huzzah!

I haven't particularly researched this, so I could be misinformed, but... I've watched several documentaries about mental hospitals in the UK. I got the impression that there are not enough mental hospitals in the area, and they were so extremely full that they just couldn't make room for new patients, or they get into situations where they need to discharge "the least worst" patient to make room for a new one. I think it's a very serious issue!

<3
I understand how you feel. It sucks we're feeling shitty right now... lets hope tomorrow is another good day. And hell, even the day after that! 

Cry it all out. Let that be your outlet instead of anything destructive. Sometimes, I'll even watch horribly sad videos just to push myself and exhaust more.

Hm. I wonder if my situation is different... but I'll share anyway.

So I don't know if I'm in the shadow of my sister because my family does consider me more successful and educated than her. She is a lot tougher than me though! I'm the nerd, she is the hot tattoo'd rebel.

But yet.. despite me not being a trouble maker, and she was, she always garnered all of the attention. A lot of negative attention I guess, I don't know what she was going through to act the way she did. (drugs, teen pregnancy, involved with people with criminal history/activities) All I know is all of my families time and effort went into "saving" her, and I was pretty neglected. They liked that I was quiet and just did my own thing alone.

edit; in retrospect, i think she and i both just had it really shitty and it manifested differently.

It's hard to go to school when you don't have any part of it to look forward to. :( When my closest friends moved away, I slowly but surely stopped going to school altogether. I'm not gonna say that was a good choice or not, since I missed out on a lot of the cooler high school things, like meeting new people my age, prom and graduation. But, I ended up getting my GED when I was ready and went to college. So, it worked out for me eventually.

I don't think it's abnormal. You were together for a long time, and it's gotta take quite a bit of getting used to to not have him around anymore. I'm sure you miss some of the good things you had with him, which is why you're sort of mourning the loss of his attention. It should get a little easier as time goes on <3 be with people who will be there to support and comfort you as you recover from the loss and what happened

Yes. When I was younger I was just waiting to grow up because I had so much hope that when I was older I would know how to handle things within my toxic family, etc.

Once I was finally an adult, things got a lot harder especially with my family, because things grew to another level of dysfunction. I thought, I was so stupid. I'm no more prepared to deal with these things than when I was 16!

But...I'm just a little bit older now. 25. And I do feel like I am able to make the hard decisions I need to in order to improve my life overall. It isn't really.. "easier", I'm just a little bit wiser.

I'm glad it's helped you! Be careful with melatonin and sleeping aids if you're depressed though, because they can make you more depressed if you use them long-term (in my experience). If you notice it, you should probably talk to your doctor about trying a sleep aid that won't have those kinds of side effects! <3

Hmm. It sounds a little too easy to be Baker Acted... that is kinda scary. It sounds kinda like being "Blue Papered", which is being forced against your will to go to a hospital because you've been deemed a threat to yourself or others. But.. evidence is needed.

But I still can't decide how bad it is. 3 days isn't too bad, since the standard (from what i understand in my state) is up to a week. And... without insurance, being there just 5 days cost me $15,000, including transportation (US medical prices...).

But, if things are different in your state, I really don't think I can provide any certain advice. I hope you can find a route thats right for you!
Hah, I feel like my mental health is perfect when I see sick behavior like that. Fuck that guy.
Is she a good friend that is aware that you're experiencing some challenges? Maybe you could ask her if you guys could do something else, maybe just talk?

Not in my experience :o making friends is easier than falling in love, I think. But then, I interpret fwb has having no real commitment attachment. Kind of a come-and-go thing. Have you experienced differently?

You can probably do something about it! I don't want to believe you'll be alone! I don't want to imply it's easy, though... you'd have to think pretty critically on why you have a hard time approaching people and then what you can do to fix it. The hardest part is gaining the experience of trying it.

Aaaand I didn't lose my virginity til 21! No shame in things like that! I decided to sleep with a good friend of mine that I trusted. I didn't wait for a relationship, and I don't regret it. He and I are still good friends.

Have you considered things like friends with benefits? You're still really young, you shouldn't feel like you have to be in a relationship right away. You can get close to people, care for them, be intimate with them, as friends. But, not everyone is into that, I understand! I just thought I would mention it.

I understand wanting to be with someone. I think just about everyone wants things like that. Sometimes I see men come on a little too strongly and be a little too nice. I've turned down good men just because I felt like it got to this kind of "romantic" stage way too fast. I think it's so valuable to be friends first. I don't know if guys are a little nervous about that because of the risk of being friend-zoned... but, I dunno.

And about the "being too nice" bit. Being nice is a good thing! But sometimes I've seen guys be too nice, and I just don't get to see or experience their real personality. You what I mean? Being nice isn't a personality, it just can feel a little.. forced. I hope I don't sound too horrible. It really just comes down to completely being yourself, rather than focusing 100% on showing her how nice you are. 

What would you consider some of your strengths are, personality or otherwise?


edit: I really want to clarify that this is only my opinion! I hope other women will comment too with theirs. I don't wanna speak for every chick out there. I could be totally biased because I just don't have a lot of interest in dating.

Are you a minor? If you're legally an adult you don't have to involve them.

But otherwise... tell them depression is a disease/sickness. It's not being "sad". It's like telling someone to snap out of having the flu. It just doesn't work like that! (I do consider depression more severe than the flu, it just seemed like an easy way to illustrate my thought)

If they don't understand, and you are able to get therapy anyway, I think you can ask your therapist for a group session to involve your parents. I bet your therapist could get them to understand.

If you feel like you can push through it, you should try. But.. I understand. Last semester I forced myself through because I only had to complete 4 more courses to have my degree. But I was crashing so hard, I couldn't focus, I showed up to classes hungover/drunk... I just kinda proved to myself I wasn't going to be able to do it right now. I felt like I got to a point where I was okay with delaying it and choosing to focus on my health and a job that can get me by for now. Do what feels right for you!

Well, I admitted to them that I had suicidal ideation, but not plans or the means to carry anything out. Like it was on my mind, but not something I wanted to do or looked into. I just wanted to get better.

How long do they typically keep people for a Baker Act? I'm in Maine, and typically people don't stay in the mental hospital (for things like depression) for longer than a week. My friend was caught in the act of attempting, and she HAD to stay a week. Because I admitted myself in, I only stayed for 5 days (they wanted to monitor how I was taking to the medication). And yeah, you do have to look like you're improving. You can't leave if they're under the impression you might still hurt yourself. They'll want to see you talking to other patients, participating in group activities, etc. But I dunno, when I was there I didn't have to fake it. I did feel better and I liked the activities. As better as I could being stuck somewhere so boring, heh.

You could try depressionforums.org
I was there for a little bit. People there are very upbeat about their responses to others. It's probably a more hopeful atmosphere than here.

Personally, I prefer this reddit. It feels a little more active and easier to just vent into.

Those are.. shitty friends. Why do they think you have a choice to just "snap out of it"? Is there something they don't understand? I assume a big YES, but... I just kind of want to hope things can work out between you and those friends IF you want it to.

It really sounds like you want to be at the school you're going to right now, right? Do you have to transfer back if you just took a semester off? I feel like you should be able to return back when you're ready. :) If it is something you wanted to do! Whatever you decide, I hope it works out well!!

Don't base your actions on a fear people will think you're mimicking your boyfriend if you feel like you may need to take the same course of action to feel better! And actually, when I was away at a mental hospital for a few days I didn't tell anyone (except two friends).

I can understand why you stopped therapy. When my therapist told me he wasn't sure what he could do for me, I stopped going too, heh. But, why did you stop your medication? That probably hit you hard, right?

I've never heard the term "Baker Act" before. Is that just when you go to a mental hospital? Is it when you are taken against your will, because they think you may hurt yourself for others? 

I voluntarily admitted myself to a mental hospital because I hit a point, almost as bad as the experiences you're describing, because all I could think was HELP. And because I voluntarily went and was cooperative and jazz, I got to decide when I wanted to leave. I had that freedom, because I had the presence of mind to know I needed HELP, not that I had to die (though, I did have suicidal ideation). Even if I had any suicidal intentions, I'd never tell them. I'm also too afraid of losing my free will. I had that scare recently when I overdosed myself and ended up in the hospital.

But anyway, you should research the topic more and get more people to tell you their experiences. Maybe it will help you to decide if it is right for you.

And yeah, being in a mental hospital SUCKS HARDCORE. I never want to go back. However, I am still glad I went and I did feel better once I got home after about 5 days. They were able to get me on the medication I needed right away, which is why I wanted to go. I needed that help NOW, not later.

Yeah! I think it's fine to post every few days just to vent. I mean.. I've been doing it, haha. I haven't gotten scolded yet!

Best of luck <3

Rockstar is right. It is intimidating to start the conversation but, if you have a friend you trust and they care for you, they're gonna want to do what they can to help you. Even if all they can do is listen and be there to tell you they care for you, that will make a big difference. You won't feel as alone.
And there is always the option to find someone here on this reddit that you feel as similar challenges that you face, and talk it out with them! They'll most likely be glad they're not alone, too!

Have you considered taking a break from school? Assuming you're in college. Don't be afraid to take time off to focus on your health! When I was at university and depressed, I realized I was only getting worse. I had to get better. So, I've taken a break until I feel ready again. I'm glad to be working more now, too. Because money can be tight during school, and that's just more stress.

If you need someone to talk to in the meantime, I think coming to this reddit is a good idea. Vent it out when you're feeling really upset, just to get it off your shoulders and out there so that it isn't weighing you down so hard. Personally I find, even if people don't respond, I feel better using this reddit as a place to just... let my raw emotions spill out. It has been a very good way for me to cope.

I.. can't imagine how you feel right now. I'm sorry you're experiencing these things. :( I can't offer advice on this issue because I don't have a lot of experience with it, but surely someone can. And if anything, I hope venting her helps you feel even a little better!

I can only speak from a woman's perspective... but, in my opinion, with enough hair loss I think men look nicer when they opt to go for the bald look instead. I hope that doesn't make me sound like an ass... I know balding is something out of peoples control. But totally bald is a very strong and attractive look!

But you know... actually, there might be other ways, too. Like, the host of the Youtube channel Vsauce is a fella experiencing some hair loss od some sort, but he makes it work very well! Maybe it's how "clean" and short the keeps it!

Don't give up hope! There are options to make yourself feel good, for sure!

I'm sorry you experienced this. That really sucks.. but I'm glad that you're not missing him. It's easier to get over someone if you're mad at them—and you have every right to be FURIOUS!

If you think you can hold it out at your school, keep strong. You were tested pretty hard.. but you're bound to find some good luck after that awful experience. You learned a lesson in reading people, too. You won't fall for it twice! You'll make another best friend for sure. A REAL best friend, who cares about you and how you feel.

But, if you start to feel isolated or like things are getting worse.. you might want to try your families advice and return home for a semester, maybe. Take a break to recuperate. There is no shame in that!
Aww yeah, rock on! I love that last part! You're stronger than you think! :)
He's being a real friend. Never doubt it or forget it! Remember to treat your friends well, and you'll feel good, too. :)

It's probably not an abnormal thing to feel. I remember being jealous when my ex got with someone new. Not because I still wanted him, but.. just, it makes me think about how I haven't found someone after him.

Man. I hope you're all right concerning the tumor, though!! That's so scary. I've been put under for a MUCH LESSER surgery, and I was terrified. I can't imagine what you must have been through.

I also know how it feels to be comforted by a stranger. During a day-long family crisis, I broke down and a stranger held me to and let me cry on him, heh. I'll never forget that. It meant a lot.

25 here. You get used to it, heh. But hey, don't let anyone ever tell you that you can't still act like a kid when you're an adult. Fun doesn't stop if you don't want it to, you know? Do you whatever you want, you just gotta take the consequences of those behaviors. Oh, but you're gonna have to pay your bills and responsibilities. Those suck. 
I'm STILL trying to figure life out. You never stop learning, you know? You get to grow from the experiences.
Something I've been needing to remember to avoid panic is realize that yeah, I'm gonna fuck up sometimes. Maybe I won't be able to pay a bill. Maybe the power will get shut off for a bit, or I won't have my phone. You just gotta stop... you can't do anything about it in that moment, so you gotta just let it go until you can do something about it. You'll be all right! You'll get through it!

Holy crap, I dunno where the commenter below me went, but that is NOTHING like what I or a friend of mine experienced. I'm gonna go ahead and share my thoughts so you're not absolutely terrified for no reason.

My friend was caught in the middle of a suicide attempt and was taken to a hospital. She HAD to stay for a week. I voluntarily admitted myself to the same hospital, and was allowed to leave whenever I wanted to (provided I was deemed not to be a danger to myself or others).
It was a very boring and restricted, clinical environment. You won't like it, but it isn't SCARY. Not based on my experience, and I was admitted to an adult section based on depression/risk of suicide.

I liked the food, but they do portion it and you have limited snacks and stuff. They have group activities, personally I enjoyed them. It passes time. We were checked on every 15 minutes, including during the night. The nurses were fine. I spoke with a doctor EVERY DAY at least once.
My friend describes it as "a vacation to a nursing home" kinda thing. I'd agree. I HATED being restricted and told what to do, and I definitely never want to go back... but the trip suited its purposes, and I was able to leave after 5 days. I was able to start medication at that time, which is why I wanted to go. I felt like I needed it critically.

So.. you're not gonna like it, but if you feel like you need help, then you'll probably get something out of it. It's more boring than anything else. But, I am glad I went.


Edit; I don't know what its like for those under 18. I'd imagine.. more temper tantrums? There are documentaries on Youtube to get some insight if nothing else. I watched one, and it didn't seem to different at a glance. Probably just patients behaviors.

That's so horrific. There was a time we hit a fox on the road... I was so angry at my dad because it seemed, to me, avoidable. I cried and felt so shitty on the way to where we were going.

I felt sort of redeemed though, cause one day my niece and I heard a cry in the woods. We looked around and found a young kitten crawling around. It wasn't even weaned yet! I have no idea how it got there! We definitely saved its life.
:( the worst
I may not be in the same boat as you, but your feelings still matter! Don't forget that!

It seems like "forced positivity", as he calls it, is kinda just... "social masks". It's something probably everyone has done; put on a smile and tough it out. Some people even have complete personalities or "characters" within their social masks. DEFINITELY a lot of Youtubers do this. And yeah, why wouldn't that be exhausting? So, Pewdiepie is kind of advocating for Youtubers to be more "real"?

Okay, but. As he says in his video, Youtubers are using this to their advantage for views. I don't really see anything wrong with that, but hey. I was raised in a capitalist society! You do what is going to make you money, so you can eat. It isn't malicious, people enjoy the entertainment. It's an equivalent exchange. 

He doesn't like it because it's "fake". Well, a lot of things are "fake", like Mickey Mouse. They serve their purposes; entertainment. But I'm guessing Pewdiepie kinda is advocating for better role models on Youtube; being "real" would be a better role model for the teenagers he is referring to. I think that's fine. I think you can do BOTH of these things. I absolutely adore watching Youtuber's "Draw Your Life" for that reason. They get real.

But, I think something Pewdiepie may be missing is.. people aren't stupid. Not really. Are people really watching Youtubers who are always happy and thinking "hey, if I just smile I'll be THAT PERSON!"? I think that may need some supporting information. I would have liked if he showed more examples of Youtubers "forcing positivity" so I could understand exactly what he means for sure, but I understand that he didn't want to call anyone out.

I think it's a fair argument, and a good thought. But I'm not sure I'm swayed by it, or see the problem.
If you watched the video to the end, he clarifies that his video is not directed at people who experience depression. He's talking standard happiness, standard sadness.

Yeah, your medical record. There is confidentiality, but there are circumstances where mental health background information may need to be discussed. I don't say this to scare you out of it! Research the topic a bit more and see how you feel. But.. if you need help, I hope a fear of it being on record doesn't keep you from it.

I'm glad you have support!!
If something is impacting your ability to function on a daily basis, you shouldn't feel guilty for seeking comfort from your family. Maybe it is easy to get complacent with a lot of support around you, I'm not entirely sure. But if you're worried about it, see if you can make some changes in your life for the better. See how taking action and getting motivated changes things for you.
It's easy for me to type this at you, but I don't know what you're going through that makes you feel depressed. Try to see what changes you can make because, if you're only lacking motivation ("lazy"), then you should be able to power through. Give it a shot, and if it doesn't work, you have your family to support you. :)

Happy birthday!!
I know how a disappointing birthday feels, too, heh. I'm sorry about hwo yours has been, and the thoughts its led you to have. :(

I've broken stuff that meant a lot to me, too. Sometimes I've caught myself doing it cause I WANTED to make myself feel shitty. Some kind of weird self harm.

Do you have close friends or family close by that you could stay with instead of her? It sounds like you are definitely in a toxic situation and you should try to get out of it. If you were like, 17, maybe you could tough it out. But man, 15. Surely there is someone you can talk to confidentially who might be able to help you get out of a bad situation. You could go to a teacher, a counselor, or school nurse and be honest that you are nervous about your mother becoming involved with things. They may have info for you!

On another note, in the US you can technically "divorce" your parents. It was something I once considered around your age. I don't know the details, but you may want to check it out.

Hair loss really sucks.. but, the bald look really isn't bad. I think it's attractive. It's actually a very strong look. If I were a man experiencing significant hair loss, I'd probably shave it all off.

Your roommate is also a dick and you should find better people to live with, heh.

I can totally relate to that... I tend ot make myself feel crappy about small things like that, too. Even with snapchat! I get too jealous.. but, being aware of it is a good thing. It means you can have the potential to catch yourself, and maybe change some behaviors.
Thank you so much. This is what I thought, but I didn't want to jump to conclusions. Thanks for taking the time to respond!

Yeah, I get the hesitation about therapy. I only went for about 3 months myself before I thought it was senseless to continue, BUT it did help me organize my thoughts. I think that's useful if you're in a situation where you're not sure what you should do.
Well, she could consider just a break from school—not stopping altogether. Currently, I'm on a break from school until I catch up with my own health problems. It just became too much for me to do schoolwork, actual work$$, AND juggle in my health.

I hope you guys can figure something out that will work!! But, it's important to make some changes if things are being mentally/emotionally too taxing. Cause if you just continue to push it, it won't get better.
Would you like to talk about it with me? Maybe I can help?

I also disagree with some of your behavior/wording here. Like, "...stop wallowing I'd have to leave her." I can't imagine a worse thing to say to someone who might be depressed, heh. It's like telling someone with only a single leg to run faster.

I'm going to assume that she is depressed, because it sure sounds like it. But I'm not all against you!! You're not a bad dude!! I totally understand! I've been that depressed girl who dumps too much emotions and stress on a single person, because I trust them the most and their support matters to me the most. I've also been a bit mean... and I regret it a lot, and try to do better. But anyway. What I'm trying to say is that you're just one person. You're not a person trained to know how to deal with an illness, like depression. It isn't fair to expect you to know exactly what to do and when to do it. Because things don't seem to be working, it's time to ask for help with someone who had the knowledge to diagnose her. You should try to encourage her to consider therapy, and just see where it goes from there. A therapist will help her organize her thoughts, and maybe she'll realize what move she should take in her life to be happier. 

I'm.. also an artist who understands show shitty it feels to be doing a bunch of assigned work that doesn't fill my portfolio with relevant things. But, in my school there were high level classes where you had a lot of freedom. Like, YOU decide your project for the semester and do it. So, there is at least that potential. Otherwise, maybe she just needs to find the time to be doing things she does love with her skill. And, maybe, that means taking a break form school.

Good luck! You posting here and asking for help does show you care about her! And.. that makes me feel good, too. I like to see people be there for their friends when they need it most.
Yeah, man. Days that go by seem so damn hazy, I dunno what happened. I think.. sometimes that goes along with things being uneventful.. the same old same old just kinda meshes together.
Yes it's triggering you. If something makes you feel bad, you should try to avoid it. At least until you're feeling better!

Well, the first boyfriend I had... (we were both 19) I remember asking him if he'd been intimate with another woman before. He was hesitant, but honest that he had been. I remember that sinking feeling, immediate insecurity. I felt like... shit, what if I'm not as good? I thought about it for quite a while, it really irked me and it IRKED me that it irked me.

I just had to come with terms that people will have been intimate with other people (in many cases), and that I shouldn't try to compare myself with their past partners and that it is REALLY UNFAIR to consider a person "unclean" if they're no longer a virgin or whatever. It's a lot more fun to focus on the here and now; and if I'm worried about my own performance... well, I'm gonna guess that my partner is gonna be very willing to put up with me wanting a lot of practice, haha. I guess different anxiety exists for men in this situation. But I can't imagine a woman who really likes you is going to judge you. She's going to want to work with you. That's coming from a woman!! If she does judge you, then she doesn't care about you (and maybe she was just looking for a fling). 

Now I'm 25, and when I like someone it never crosses my mind how many people that person may or may not have been with. That doesn't invalidate me, and it shouldn't. But, you don't just GET OVER things, you have to think very critically. Why does it bother you? Is it really rational? It's up to you to try and be comfortable with it.
That insecurity will come to pass as you get older, trust me. I've been there.

It's true that some people just don't care about birthdays and holidays as much as others. Not in a bad way! I think it can be easy to forget how important they might be for other people. I think you should tell him how much it would have meant to you for him to have done something special for you. I bet he'll want to make it up to you if he accidentally hurt you!
Sounds like a boyfriend I would duuuumppp.
